entries.name: Fully visible sigmoid belief network
entries.definition: A fully observed binary autoregressive probabilistic model whose conditional probability at each position is a logistic function of a bias and a weighted sum of preceding visible variables.
entries.identity_notes: This is the fully visible sigmoid model discussed by Larochelle and Murray, with no stochastic hidden variables. Frey and colleagues call their binary logistic special case a fully visible belief network; that local usage does not make all fully visible Bayesian networks synonyms of the sigmoid family. The record specializes the broader sigmoid-belief-network family and is distinct from NADE’s nonlinear deterministic hidden features and DARN’s stochastic latent architecture. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 346 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 23 and 23 lines respectively. All 17 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: SBN source metadata, NADE and DARN scope distinctions, their saved review and the carried noisy-OR discovery lead, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Seventeen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The chain-rule factorization is general, but restricting each conditional to a logistic-linear function limits the distribution family. A given fixed-order conditional table with a nonzero logit interaction cannot be represented by that affine logit; this is not a claim about every alternative ordering or latent extension.

Exact complete-observation likelihood and forward generation do not provide arbitrary missing-variable posteriors for free. Conditioning on a suffix while earlier variables are unknown still requires inference or summation.

Changing the variable order changes the restricted model family and can affect fitting. The absence of stochastic latent variables is part of this specialization, not a property of all sigmoid belief networks.

The source’s FVBN label is interpreted within its binary logistic model setting. No assertion that every fully visible Bayesian model uses logistic factors, no universal performance ranking and no trained-model result is included.

claims.statement: Fix an ordering of D binary visible variables. Parameterize P(x_i=1|x_<i)=sigmoid(b_i+sum_(j<i) w_ij x_j). Multiply the corresponding Bernoulli probabilities over positions to evaluate the normalized observed joint. All variables in that product are visible, so complete-data likelihood evaluation has no hidden-state marginalization or recognition-model posterior approximation. Its negative log likelihood is the sum of the positionwise binary logistic losses. Generate a sample by drawing each bit from the conditional determined by already drawn predecessors. Full connectivity makes all earlier visible variables available as parents; zero coefficients can remove particular dependencies. A fixed-order conditional’s log odds are affine in its predecessors, unlike the more general nonlinear neural conditional used by NADE.

entries.name: Noisy-OR belief network
entries.definition: A directed acyclic binary probabilistic network that models a node’s inactivity as the product of a leak-failure factor and failure factors for its active parents.
entries.identity_notes: The core record denotes the noisy-OR conditional model described by Neal, with zero/one variables and failure factors between zero and one. It is a probabilistic conditional family, not additive input noise, a deterministic OR gate or a sigmoid function. Neal also studies a signed-weight exponential extension; its distinct validity condition and loss of an individual failure-probability interpretation are stated explicitly rather than silently treating negative weights as ordinary noisy-OR failures. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 346 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 23 and 23 lines respectively. All 17 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: SBN source metadata, NADE and DARN scope distinctions, their saved review and the carried noisy-OR discovery lead, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Seventeen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: A negative weighted input gives an invalid negative activation probability. The signed extension therefore needs explicit constraints and is not an unconstrained sigmoid parameterization.

Zero failure probabilities yield deterministic activation contributions and infinite log-failure weights; the probability-product form still defines the boundary, but the finite-weight reparameterization excludes those endpoints.

The independent-failure interpretation concerns contributions conditional on parent states, not a proof that the parent variables are independent or that the model’s edges identify interventions in real data.

Local normalization and ancestral generation do not remove hidden-variable marginalization or guarantee Gibbs mixing. Boundary zero probabilities can also obstruct positivity conditions used by sampling arguments.

Neal’s constraint-projection and learning discussion was inspected, but its appendix proofs and executable implementations were not audited. No projection-optimality theorem, general convergence or empirical advantage is certified.

claims.statement: For node i, let q_i0 be the failure probability for an always-on bias or leak source and q_ij the failure probability associated with active parent j. Set P(s_i=0|parents)=q_i0 times the product of q_ij over parents with state1, and set P(s_i=1|parents) to its complement. This corresponds to independently failing activation contributions; it does not require the parent variables themselves to be independent. Multiply normalized node factors in a topological order to obtain the joint model and sample it ancestrally. For strictly positive failure factors, define w_ij=-log(q_ij), including the bias; then P(s_i=1|parents)=1-exp(-a_i), with a_i=w_i0+sum_j w_ij s_j and nonnegative standard weights. Neal’s separate signed-weight extension retains this exponential formula if a_i is nonnegative for every binary parent configuration, equivalently w_i0+sum_(j:w_ij<0) w_ij>=0. Negative weights in that extension need not correspond to failure probabilities in[0,1]. Parameter updates must preserve validity; the architecture itself does not specify a unique learning algorithm.

entries.name: Order-agnostic NADE training
entries.definition: A stochastic training procedure that shares neural conditional parameters across variable orderings and estimates the order-averaged NADE log-likelihood objective using a sampled observed prefix and losses for all remaining variables.
entries.identity_notes: This is Uria, Murray and Larochelle’s order-agnostic training procedure, applicable to shallow or deep NADE and its real-valued extension. It is distinct from the original fixed-order NADE architecture, the existence of additional deterministic hidden layers alone, and an ensemble mixture evaluated after training. Parameter sharing across orderings does not assert that every ordering defines the same joint distribution. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 346 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 23 and 23 lines respectively. All 17 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: SBN source metadata, NADE and DARN scope distinctions, their saved review and the carried noisy-OR discovery lead, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Seventeen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Shared parameters do not force order-specific joint distributions to agree. Choosing an ordering convenient for a conditioning query performs inference under that chosen member, not necessarily under another ordering or the ensemble mixture.

Conditioning an ensemble generally reweights its members by their evidence probabilities. Uniformly choosing a member after observing evidence does not automatically sample the ensemble posterior; a finite curator example checks this distinction.

The unbiased prefix estimator depends on the stated uniform ordering/prefix sampling and D/(D-d+1) weighting. Arbitrary masks, unweighted missing-output losses or nonuniform prefix sampling require a corresponding derivation.

The presence mask is additional input information, not a sequence-timestep skipping layer or a guarantee that missing-data mechanisms have been modeled. The paper distinguishes its missing-output loss from ordinary denoising-autoencoder reconstruction.

The training objective is an average of log probabilities rather than the log of an average probability. Ensemble density evaluation costs and deep full-joint evaluation differ from one stochastic training update; selecting a convenient model is not dimension-independent numerical inference.
No agreement of all conditionals with one joint distribution, universal performance gain, global optimization guarantee or complete implementation audit is asserted.

claims.statement: Treat a variable ordering o as uniformly distributed over permutations and minimize the mean over data and o of the negative log probability assigned by the corresponding autoregressive NADE. For a training example, sample an ordering and a prefix length d-1 uniformly from zero through D-1. Feed the observed prefix values to the shared neural conditional network, set unobserved input values to zero and append a binary mask identifying observed dimensions so that observed zeros remain distinguishable from missing inputs. Evaluate the conditional loss for each of the D-d+1 remaining variables under that same prefix, sum those losses and multiply by D/(D-d+1). The resulting loss and, under the differentiability conditions, its gradient estimate the order-averaged objective; one masked-prefix forward/backward computation serves all missing outputs. Additional deterministic hidden layers can be used, while full joint evaluation for a chosen ordering still requires all ordered conditionals. After training, a selected ordering defines one normalized autoregressive model. A separate ensemble averages the joint probabilities of selected orderings, and samples by selecting a member then generating from that member. This probability average is distinct from the order-average log-likelihood training objective.

source_interpretations: The order-agnostic expected negative log density objective is not the negative log density of the ensemble mixture.

Sample a uniform prefix length and ordering, mask inputs, and scale the sum of remaining-variable losses by D/(D-d+1); this estimates the order-average objective. Observed-value mask distinguishes observed zeros from omitted variables.

Different orderings with shared parameters need not define the same joint distribution. Choosing a convenient ordering for a query is inference under that member, not arbitrary exact inference under every member or the mixture.

A mixture generates by first choosing one component ordering then ancestral sampling that component. Conditioning a mixture generally changes component weights; uniform component selection after evidence is not automatically posterior mixture sampling.

Deep training can reuse one masked-prefix forward pass for all missing outputs; evaluating a full ordered joint still takes D conditionals. The source phrase constant time concerns selecting the convenient model, not dimension-independent numerical inference.

Standard noisy-OR failure products with bias/leak have nonnegative log-failure weights. Neal’s signed extension keeps probabilities valid only when the minimum weighted input is nonnegative; negative link weights no longer individually correspond to failure probabilities in[0,1]. The extension is explicitly distinguished from the standard independent-failure interpretation.

The fully visible sigmoid model is logistic-linear for each fixed-order prefix conditional and has no latent posterior to infer for complete observations. Removing hidden variables restricts representational scope but allows exact observed joint evaluation. Missing observed variables still require appropriate conditional inference.

The finite noisy-OR conditional has nonzero logit interaction and is not logistic-linear in the two fixed-order parent variables. This is a conditional-family distinction, not an exhaustive proof about every possible variable ordering.

Fix an ordering of D binary observations. For each position i compute h_i=sigmoid(c+W[:,<i] x_<i) and r_i=P(x_i=1|x_<i)=sigmoid(b_i+V[i,:] h_i). The joint probability is the product over i of r_i raised to x_i times (1-r_i) raised to (1-x_i). Initialize the hidden preactivation accumulator a_1=c and update a_(i+1)=a_i+W[:,i] x_i after evaluating position i. This reuses prefix work and supports O(DH) evaluation for the original one-hidden-layer construction with H hidden units. Train by differentiating the exact average negative log joint probability. claims.statement: Choose a topological ordering of binary nodes and directed connections from earlier parents to later nodes. In zero/one encoding let a_i=b_i+sum_j w_ij s_j over parents; then P(s_i=1|parents)=sigmoid(a_i) and P(s_i=0|parents)=1-sigmoid(a_i). Multiplying these locally normalized factors gives the joint distribution without an undirected global partition function. Ancestral sampling visits nodes in topological order. For the equivalent minus-one/plus-one encoding, divide each non-bias weight by two and add half the original incoming-weight sum to the original bias. Marginalizing hidden variables still requires a sum over their configurations, and a Gibbs full conditional uses both the node factor and factors of its children, rather than merely its forward conditional. In the inspected maximum-likelihood learning derivation, gradients of a visible-data log likelihood are posterior expectations of joint log-probability scores; Gibbs sampling is one approximation for those expectations, not a mandatory part of the architecture.

claims.statement: During wake, present an observed input and sample its hidden representation layer by layer through the bottom-up recognition distribution q_phi(h|x). Hold recognition parameters fixed for this update and ascend log p_theta(x,h) in the generative parameters. For the original Bernoulli-sigmoid units, a generative weight receives a learning-rate-scaled product of its sampled parent state and the difference between the sampled target state and the generative activation probability; biases use a constant parent. During sleep, sample a full configuration (x,h) ancestrally from the current top-down generative model, then ascend log q_phi(h|x) in the recognition parameters while holding generative parameters fixed. The generated lower-layer states serve as inputs and their known sampled upper-layer causes as targets. This also gives local Bernoulli delta rules in the original parameterization. The wake update follows the generative-parameter variational-bound gradient at fixed q; the sleep update instead fits recognition on model-generated inputs and targets the posterior-to-recognition KL direction averaged under model inputs. The two phases are not generally gradients of the same data ELBO.
